text:
maria (devex): quick report from a customer onboarding today: their sample-app started failing after they rotated a staging key. we reproduced: app 401s, SDK auto-refresh succeeds, but requests get routed to wrong project. throwing this here to capture fixes and docs.

aj (sdk): can you show the exact env layout they used? different customers mix REDWOOD_PROJECT vs REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID etc.

maria (devex): they used REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT=tenant-42. CLI login was used by dev to seed session, then a rotation happened in portal. After rotation SDK got new token but outgoing requests omitted x-rwd-project; backend picked org default and returned permission denied.

leo (cli): I dug in. CLI's session write path previously wrote only token + org in ~/.redwood/session.json. we never persisted project. when users run `rwd login` without `--project`, we used env REDWOOD_PROJECT until refresh replaced session store. if sample-app relied on the session file for state it loses project on refresh.

samir (platform): two layers: 1) naming is messy (REDWOOD_PROJECT vs REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID vs REDWOOD_DEFAULT_PROJECT) 2) refresh semantics drop per-client headers. I'd like us to standardize env naming and ensure the refresh flow preserves client-level metadata.

jen (support): recommend we treat precedence as: explicit request opts > CLI flags > env vars > session fallback > account defaults. customers keep getting surprised when CLI changes behavior after login.

aj (sdk): agreed. SDK change proposal: add Session.metadata map persisted to disk (project, request_headers, created_at). On refresh, SDK should reapply Session.metadata before retrying the original request. I'll add hooks so Go/JS/Python SDKs share tests.

leo (cli): CLI changes: add `--project` flag on login and login should write project into session.metadata when available. Also add migration so existing sessions without metadata preserve env-provided project. I'll open a PR tonight.

maria (devex): can we also make env var naming explicit in docs? customers used REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID and it silently worked in older SDKs but not in latest. let's pick one canonical var.

samir (platform): pick REDWOOD_PROJECT, keep the legacy names supported for 6 months but warn at startup if legacy var present. Backend will also accept x-rwd-project header and we will not accept project claims from token until we have a rollout plan.

aj (sdk): test matrix note: ensure streaming and long-poll endpoints don't lose headers mid-stream if a refresh occurs. also test ephemeral key rotation where both old+new keys coexist for a short period.

jen (support): I'll update KB with a troubleshooting snippet and `rwd login --show-session` sample. include sample migration command to copy legacy env var into session: `rwd login --project "$REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID"`.

ops-bot: rotation event recorded: key pk_staging_77 rotated at 2080123500. impacted tokens invalidated 2080123520 -> 2080123580.

maria (devex): action items: aj -> SDK session.metadata patch + tests (ETA 48 hrs). leo -> CLI flag+migration + prefer flag>env>session (ETA 24 hrs). samir -> env var deprecation plan + server-side token-claim roadmapping (sync Fri). jen -> KB edits + support playbook (ETA tomorrow).

leo (cli): note for UX: prefer explicit flag, then env, then session. will log a warning if session has conflicting project.

aj (sdk): starting cross-language tests now. will include a unit that simulates rotation and asserts request headers preserved and a log line `auth: refreshed token, preserving project=tenant-42` appears.

samir (platform): I'll add a server metric for "rotation-induced 401 spike" so we can monitor regressions.

maria (devex): thanks team. once PRs land I'll update the sample-app quickstart to demonstrate resilient rotation: set `REDWOOD_PROJECT`, show `rwd login --project`, and verify `rwd login --show-session`.
